title: Vital Information About Wills, Trusts, and Estate Plans
location: https://mackaydressler.com/workshops
description:
Creating your estate plan, whether it’s a living trust or a will, can be a daunting task. Estate planning addresses issues that are difficult to think about, such as death, incapacity, finances, and family dynamics. It can be easy to procrastinate, even though these issues may weigh heavily on your mind.

We invite you to attend one of our upcoming free webinars so you can take the first step toward having peace of mind by creating (or updating) your estate plan. This is an educational webinar, where we highlight some of the concerns that many families face and how an estate plan can help. The attorneys also break down how wills and trusts differ, and some of the common estate planning pitfalls and how to avoid them.

Our goal is to provide you with the education you need to protect yourself and your family, and leave a legacy of peace. If you would like to set up a meeting to discuss your estate planning needs further, we offer all participants who complete the webinar a free, no obligation personal consultation with one of the attorneys.

At this webinar, we will discuss several common issues and concerns, including:

  * The advantages and disadvantages of wills, living trusts, and probate
  * Protecting your children’s inheritance from their future ex-spouses, lawsuits, and other claims
  * Most living trusts fail; if you already have a trust, find out what you can do to ensure that it will protect you and your loved ones
  * How to preserve your nest egg for your family if you find yourself needing Long Term Care
  * How to stay out of court and avoid the cost, time, and stress that a conservatorship can bring if you become incapacitated.

Attend a webinar and receive a FREE no-obligation consultation with an Attorney to answer any questions about setting up your estate plan ($550 value).

title: Happy Hour Crafts
description:
The Rebel Craft Collective
Wine + tasty snacks + your latest project and a friendly group of likeminded crafters... what better way to unwind? Come join us!

This is a relaxed, drop-in-friendly event. Come when you can, leave when you must. Newcomers and occasional-comers are always welcome!

**What do we mean by “crafts”?**
Whatever “craft” means to you! And whatever is portable enough to bring to a wine bar. Knitting, crochet, and other fiber arts are most common, but we have also warmly welcomed people who sketch, color, embroider, bead, and more. If your craft isn’t portable, we will happily ooh and aah over photos of your work-in-progress, or chat about your plans for your next project.

**Health & Safety**
Masks are very welcome, and nobody will pressure you to eat or drink. If the weather is nice, we will try to sit outside. If you aren’t eating/drinking during the event, please consider ordering some of La Dolce Vita’s delicious food to-go, in order to help support our gracious, long-time venue.

**Parking**
Parking in downtown Petaluma is free, but street parking has a strictly enforced 2 hour limit until 6pm. To park for longer, try the nearest garage:

* The Second Street Garage entrance is located on C Street between First and Second Streets. It's all day parking on every level and a short walk to La Dolce Vita.

**Ages**
It's a wine bar, so this event is for adult crafters (though you're certainly not required to drink wine!). We’re okay with babes-in-arms if you are, but this is not the right setting for wee crafters who are moving about on their own.

title: Jenner Headlands
description:
Go Wild Hikers
A good day to look for wildflowers. Jenner Headlands is a spectacular 5,630-acre mosaic of redwood and Douglas fir forests, oak woodland, chaparral, and coastal prairie overlooking the Pacific Ocean. Coastal prairie is rare and only found along the Pacific Coast of California and southern Oregon. These areas support a rich assemblage of native plants and are one of the most diverse types of grasslands in North America. Many rare and endangered species inhabit the property including the northern spotted owl, peregrine falcon, and red tree vole. Deer, bobcat, coyote, mountain lion and steelhead trout are also found on the property. A challenging hike best for individuals and dogs with at least a moderate level of fitness.

**Where We Meet/Important Directions**
Jenner Headlands Preserve
Hwy 1 Jenner, Ca
**Get there Early! Carpool if you can - This is a very Popular Park!**
Give yourself plenty of time to arrive and use restroom. It often takes longer than you think.

**Six things to remember when hiking near cattle**
1- Properly latch any gates you pass through on trails.
2- Always keep dogs on leash. Do not let pets chase or harass livestock.
Cows cannot distinguish the difference between a coyote and a dog.
3- If cattle are blocking the trail, approach them slowly, speak normally, and allow them to move away. If they don’t move away on their own, provide a wide berth by walking around them off-trail, if necessary.
4- If you see a stray calf, leave it alone; the mother is often feeding or watering nearby and will return. Do not get between a mother cow and young calves.
5- Give space to any cow that shows signs of aggression. This may mean giving them lots of space and walking off-trail if necessary.
6- If you encounter a cow that is acting in a threatening manner, or appears to be injured, sick or dead, please note the location, the color of the animal, the ear tag number, and report it to the park.
https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/Learn/Blog/Articles/Sharing-Sonoma-County-trails-with-cows/

**The Hike (Group Hike #340)**
Sea to Sky and Raptor Ridge trails - A loop hike
Length - +/-5 miles/8.1 kilometers
Elevation change - +/-950 feet/290 meters
Difficulty - 7+/10 - some steep & rocky sections and a seasonal creek crossing. Must be sure footed (confident and competent)! Bring trekking poles.
Exposure - 99% sun/1% shade - steep, rocky, maybe mud, ticks/insects, poison oak and cows.
Bring plenty of water! At least 68 oz./2 liters **\*Think Exposure\***.
Dogs - Yes, well behaved fit dogs on a leash are welcome.
Facilities at trail head - Picnic tables and restrooms.
Cost - $5 Cash.
Parking - Free but only 30 parking spaces! Overflow parking on Hwy 1.
**Get there Early! Carpool if you can - This is a very Popular Park!**
Remember to wear appropriate hiking shoes, bring plenty of water, for your dog too, a hat, snack/lunch and layered clothing.
Please Do Not Use Any scented products the day of a group hike!
Of course, we will all look out for each other but ultimately, hikers are responsible for their own safety and well-being during hikes.

**After Hike Gathering**
Café Aquatica
(One of our favorites
and dogs are allowed)
10439 CA-1, Jenner, CA 95450
https://www.cafeaquaticajenner.com/#/

**When We Meet**
Saturday April 25, 2026
8:30 am - 11:30 pm
**Get there Early! Carpool if you can - This is a very Popular Park!**
**If your plans change after you sign up even if you're on the waitlist, please update your RSVP.**
Do Not Attend if you are sick, running a fever, were exposed to or have tested positive for Covid-19 or any other contagion!
Hike may be changed, rescheduled or cancelled in case of excessive heat, rain, smoke/AQI, illness, zombie apocalypse etc... Check your email the night before for any possible changes.

**Notice to New Hikers Only**
***"When a New Hiker (never hiked with me before) doesn't show up (No Show) to their first hike with the group, they will be removed (not banned) from the group immediately."***

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

title: Mindfulness Sunday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism, and provide an opportunity to deepen mindfulness, wisdom, and inner stillness.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out the [recording from the past event](https://youtube.com/live/s07U2kzWoWk?feature=share) on our YouTube channel.
You’re also welcome to join us in person at Dhammadharini Monastery, in the peaceful setting of our outdoor Dana Sala Pavilion

title: Angel Island Hike  (Leave on Tiburon Ferry at 10:00)
description:
Mindfull Hikes
**\*\*\* 4/19/2026 Hike is full and RSVPs are closed \*\*\***
This hike is for members who have attended two or more hikes in the last three months and buy a ferry ticket. Everyone will start off on the waitlist. ***When you buy your ticket let me know and I'll move you to 'going'.*** Group size is limited to 10.

***Please be in good enough shape to hike at a moderate/fast steady pace (+/-2.5 mph) and comfortable with elevation changes.***

**Distance:** +/- 6.2 miles total
**The hike:** Venturing out from our usual hiking places to have a little fun. A loop hike along north ridge trail, ida trail, fire road and sunset trail. Exquisite views along the way from multiple perspectives.

We'll take the 10:00 AM ferry from Tiburon to Angel Island, hike and return on the 2:20 or 3:20 PM ferry from Angel Island to Tiburon.

**Where to Meet:** Caffè Acri in Tiburon at 9:27 AM

**Link to buy your ferry ticket:** https://angelislandferry.com/schedule/

**What to bring:** Lunch, water, hat, good hiking shoes, a joyful spirit and laughter. Please dress appropriately for the weather that day. Layers of clothing are always advisable.
**===================================**
**Reminders:**
Mindful hikes are intended to be a way to connect more fully with ourselves, each other and with the land. There will be two periods of silent walking throughout the hike to allow the senses to be fully alive and felt. There will also be time during the hike to visit and connect with each other. These times of talking and connecting are an invitation to bring mindfulness to the present moment. **It's a time to put away the cell phone and cameras to disengage from technology to be fully present with each other, our *senses and the land we are inhabiting.***

**Dāna**
In the spirit of the Buddhist tradition mindful hikes are offered as a dāna based event. Rick Hansen says “generosity is a beautiful practice that opens and gladdens the heart, relaxes the contraction of ‘self’ and ripples out into the world to touch many people.” The dāna practice is **heart centered** and in the spirit of generosity. Venmo or cash is graciously accepted. Venmo account is: @vickieix8; last four digits 4714 of my phone # if asked.

title: English Country Dance Napa
description:
North Bay Contra Dance
English country dancing is done in long lines (like contra), circles, or in geometric sets (squares, triangles). Like our contra dances, there is live music and a caller. You can come by yourself or with friends, since we change partners after each dance. If you’ve ever done contra or square dancing, much of our dance vocabulary will be familiar to you since both of those styles evolved from English country dancing.

The dance is held the 1st and 3rd Sundays of each month, 2-4:30 pm, to live music, all levels of experience welcome; and occasional 5th Sundays for Advanced dancers. Admission is $15 for members of NBCDS and its affiliates, $8 for young adults ages 19-30, and $3 for youth ages 6 – 18.

title: FEET IN THE MUD- WORKSHOP 3
location: Petaluma River Park Foundation, 159 H Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Stages of Chinese Exclusion: Out of the Gold Mines, Urban Factories, and Eventually from Most Back-Breaking Farm Work We may typically see the Chinese Exclusion Act as a law signed by Congress in 1882, but Chinese communities experienced exclusion since they arrived—in the mines in the 1850s, in urban factories in the 1870s, and in rural farm labor between 1880 and 1890. Through mini-lectures, hands-on activities, and group discussion, explore how these experiences ultimately shaped the California agriculture system, and why driving Chinese workers out was not a victory for white laborers. title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

title: Beginners in The Work of Byron Katie: Newcomers Welcome

title: Indian Tree in Novato
description:
Mindfull Hikes
***Please be in good enough shape to hike at a moderate/fast steady pace (+/-2.5 mph) and comfortable with elevation changes.***

**Distance:** +/- 7 miles total
**The hike:** Come explore fields of ferns, mature redwood groves, and ridge line vistas in Novato. We'll ascend through stands of redwoods and mature woodlands that open up to scenic views of Stafford Lake. The Ship’s Mast Trail takes us through a quiet redwood grove. West wind breezes and north facing slopes cloaked in oak, bay, and madrone will keep us cool if it's a hot day.

**Trails:** Big Trees Trail to Indian Tree Fire Road to Ship's mast Trail and back to the start on Big Trees Trail

**Parking:** Free along Vineyard Road

**How to get there:** From Hwy 101 in Novato, take exit 463 for San Marin Dr west 2.7 miles. San Marin Dr turns into Sutro Ave at Novato Blvd. Follow Sutro Ave 1 mile, turn right at Vineyard Rd and follow 1 mile. Trailhead is on the left where the paved road becomes a dirt road.

No restroom facilities

*Please be on time. We’ll start promptly at the start time listed.* Give yourself a little extra time to arrive and get situated so that you’re part of the opening circle as this is an essential part of our time together.

**What to bring:** Snack, water, hat, good hiking shoes, a joyful spirit and laughter. Please dress appropriately for the weather that day. Layers of clothing are always advisable.
===

***===================================***
***Reminders:***
Mindful hikes are intended to be a way to connect more fully with ourselves, each other and with the land. There will be two periods of silent walking throughout the hike to allow the senses to be fully alive and felt. There will also be time during the hike to visit and connect with each other. These times of talking and connecting are an invitation to bring mindfulness to the present moment. ***It's a time to put away the cell phone and cameras to disengage from technology to be fully present with each other, our senses and the land we are inhabiting.***

***If you're on the waitlist for the hike and want to attend please message Vickie a few days before the scheduled hike. Most hikes have people drop off at the last minute and it's possible there is an opening.***

**Dāna**
In the spirit of the Buddhist tradition mindful hikes are offered as a dāna based event. Rick Hansen says “generosity is a beautiful practice that opens and gladdens the heart, relaxes the contraction of ‘self’ and ripples out into the world to touch many people.” The dāna practice is **heart centered** and in the spirit of generosity. Venmo or cash is graciously accepted. Venmo account is: @vickieix8; last four digits 4714 of my phone # if asked.

**No-Show Policy:** Please cancel at least 24 hours before the start of the hike. Be mindful that there may be a waitlist. If your plans change and you're not coming, opening up a spot 4-5 days before the hike it's more likely someone will be able to attend than if you cancel at the last minute. You're considered a no-show if you cancel at the last minute. Members with 2 no-shows will be removed from the group.

title: Monte Rio Redwoods
description:
Go Wild Hikers
This is one of My Favorite local places to hike. There are spectacular views of the Willow Creek watershed and miles of hiking trails thru redwood forests dappled with sunlight.
**This Trailhead Has Very Limited Parking.**
**You Must Have Zero No Shows to Attend.**
**Everyone will start on the Waitlist.**
**Please Do Not just show up for this hike!!!**

**Where We Meet/Important Directions**
Due to limited parking and the desire to accommodate as many hikers as possible everyone must carpool!
**Meet and be ready to leave by \*830am\* from the commuter parking lot at the corner of Graton Rd. & Main St. in Occidental.**
Give yourself plenty of time to arrive, it often takes longer than you think. Especially this one!

**The Hike**
Fern Springs, Eastside, Deadwood, Koerber, Upper Freeze Out, Blair Witch, West Panties and East Panties trails - A loop hike
Length - +/-5.25 miles/8.45 kilometers
Elevation change - +/-985 feet/252 meters
Difficulty - 7+/10 moderately strenuous
Exposures - 40% sun /60% shade - rocky, poison oak, ticks and insects.
Bring plenty of water. At least 68 oz. /2 liters.
Dogs - No, only because we're car pooling.
Facilities at trail head - None! Plan ahead.
Cost - $5 cash
Parking - **Meet and be ready to leave by 830am from the commuter parking lot at the corner of Graton Rd. & Main St. in Occidental.**
Remember to wear appropriate hiking shoes, bring plenty of water, snack/lunch, layered clothing & trekking poles.
Please Do Not Use Any scented products the day of a group hike!
Of course, we will all look out for each other but ultimately, hikers are responsible for their own safety and well-being during hikes.

**After Hike Gathering**
Wild Flour Bakery
140 Bohemian Hwy, Freestone, CA 95472
(707) 874-2938
[https://wildflourbread.com/](https://wildflourbread.com/)

**When We Meet**
Sunday May 3, 2026
8:30 am - 12:00 pm
If your plans change after you sign up even if you're on the waitlist, please update your RSVP.
Do Not Attend if you are sick, running a fever, were exposed to or have tested positive for Covid-19 or any other contagion!
Hike may be changed, rescheduled or cancelled in case of excessive heat, rain, smoke/AQI, illness, zombie apocalypse etc... Check your email the night before for any possible changes.

title: Mindfulness Sunday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism, and provide an opportunity to deepen mindfulness, wisdom, and inner stillness.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out the [recording from the past event](https://youtube.com/live/s07U2kzWoWk?feature=share) on our YouTube channel.
You’re also welcome to join us in person at Dhammadharini Monastery, in the peaceful setting of our outdoor Dana Sala Pavilion
Register for this event on Dhammadharini's website to receive the address:

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out Dhammadharini Sangha at [https://www.dhammadharini.net/](https://www.dhammadharini.net/)

title: Free Estate Planning Webinar

description:
Creating your estate plan, whether it’s a living trust or a will, can be a daunting task. Estate planning addresses issues that are difficult to think about, such as death, incapacity, finances, and family dynamics. It can be easy to procrastinate, even though these issues may weigh heavily on your mind.

We invite you to attend one of our upcoming free webinars so you can take the first step toward having peace of mind by creating (or updating) your estate plan. This is an educational webinar, where we highlight some of the concerns that many families face and how an estate plan can help. The attorneys also break down how wills and trusts differ, and some of the common estate planning pitfalls and how to avoid them.

Our goal is to provide you with the education you need to protect yourself and your family, and leave a legacy of peace. If you would like to set up a meeting to discuss your estate planning needs further, we offer all participants who complete the webinar a free, no obligation personal consultation with one of the attorneys.

At this webinar, we will discuss several common issues and concerns, including:

  * The advantages and disadvantages of wills, living trusts, and probate
  * Protecting your children’s inheritance from their future ex-spouses, lawsuits, and other claims
  * Most living trusts fail; if you already have a trust, find out what you can do to ensure that it will protect you and your loved ones
  * How to preserve your nest egg for your family if you find yourself needing Long Term Care
  * How to stay out of court and avoid the cost, time, and stress that a conservatorship can bring if you become incapacitated.

Attend a webinar and receive a FREE no-obligation consultation with an Attorney to answer any questions about setting up your estate plan ($550 value).

Petaluma Figure Drawing Meetup Group
# [Crit Group At Suite G Studio](https://www.suitegstudio.com/eventscalendar/crit-group)

*With Guest Moderator: Petaluma Public Art Specialist- Melissa Abercrombie*

* Thursday, May 7, 2026
* 6:00 PM 9:00 PM

**Why Create Art in a Vacuum?**

Join us at Suite G Studio for our first group critique. Each artist brings one to two (within the same series) pieces, either finished or in progress, to receive feedback from other artists and a guest professional moderator. This is a fun, engaging, relaxed atmosphere to talk about your work, get the perspectives from fellow artists, while having the opportunity to learn about their work practices.
Each artist will have a 10-15 minute slot in which the moderator and artists discuss their work. They will be given 5 minutes at the end of their crit to discuss or explain their work.
Cost $30
Space is limited to 10 participants. To reserve your spot you can Venmo @suiteg $30, or [BECOME A MEMBER](https://www.suitegstudio.com/artist-resources)! for $40/month, come to all drawing groups and other events for free. However, you must still [RSVP](suitegstudio620@gmail.com) to hold your spot.

More About Melissa Abercrombie
Melissa Abercrombie is a creative fueled by community engagement. She holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Painting and Printmaking from San Francisco State University and brings artistic vision, passion, and civic commitment to every project. Her tenure as chair of the Petaluma Public Art Committee, along with service on multiple city commissions, informs her work as a Public Art Specialist focused on integrating art into public spaces and expanding opportunities for artists and residents to engage in creative expression.
Melissa’s leadership is reflected in her contributions to a diverse portfolio of public art projects that animate the City of Petaluma and strengthen its cultural identity. As the staff liaison to the Petaluma Public Art Committee, she has guided the Lucchesi Skatepark Public Art RFP for an upcoming youth-centered installation. She project-managed *Scent Me Back*, a narrative mural by Rough Edge Collective at the Petaluma Teen Center that connects memory and place, and oversaw the selection and installation of *Slough Birds*, an environmental artwork honoring local ecology by Jonny Hirschmugl. She also partnered with artist Michael Garlington to develop *True Heart of Petaluma: Ode to the Petaluma Fairgrounds #1*, a photo mural celebrating civic pride during a period of transition at the Fairgrounds. Additionally, she project-managed *Woven Stories*, an installation by Rude Calderón and Roberto Delgado amplifying Native community voices on a junior high campus.

title: Mother's Day hike - Pt Reyes - Drakes Estero Trailhead
description:
Mindfull Hikes
***Please be in good enough shape to hike at a moderate/fast steady pace (+/-2.5 mph) and comfortable with elevation changes.***

**Distance:** +/- 8.5 miles (depends how far down the beach we walk) round trip; out and back
**The hike:** We'll hike the Estero and Sunset Beach trails to our turn around point. This trail through grassland and cattle pastures offers outstanding views of Drakes Estero and Estero de Limantour, and the opportunity to see the diverse wildlife that call these ecosystems home.

**Where to meet:** Estero Trailhead
https://www.google.com/maps/place/Drakes+Estero+Trailhead/@38.0818337,-122.9166303,17z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x8085d00e42f7135d:0xbcebd32f56666a3e!8m2!3d38.0818295!4d-122.9140554!16s%2Fg%2F11bxc61t29?entry=ttu

The Estero Trailhead parking lot is approximately 20 minutes by car from the Bear Valley Visitor Center. There is a small dirt parking lot with space for \~30 vehicles on the west side of Home Ranch Road one mile (1.6 km) from Sir Francis Drake Boulevard. The Home Ranch Road is only one lane wide and does not have many good places to pull off. Drive slowly and cautiously. **Tip:** There are road signs at all major intersections along the way indicating which way to turn to get to the Lighthouse. Follow the signs for "Lighthouse" until you see a sign for the Estero trailhead.

*Please be on time. We’ll start promptly at the start time listed.* ***Give yourself a little extra time to arrive*** and get situated so that you’re part of the opening circle as this is an essential part of our time together.

**Parking:** Free

**Restroom**: At the trailhead

**What to bring:** Lunch, water, hat, good hiking shoes, a joyful spirit and laughter. Please dress appropriately for the weather that day. Layers of clothing are always advisable.
**===================================**
**Reminders:**
Mindful hikes are intended to be a way to connect more fully with ourselves, each other and with the land. There will be two periods of silent walking throughout the hike to allow the senses to be fully alive and felt. There will also be time during the hike to visit and connect with each other. These times of talking and connecting are an invitation to bring mindfulness to the present moment. **It's a time to put away the cell phone and cameras to disengage from technology to be fully present with each other, our *senses and the land we are inhabiting.***

***If you're on the waitlist for the hike and want to attend please message Vickie a few days before the scheduled hike. Most hikes have people drop off at the last minute and it's possible there is an opening.***

**Dāna**
In the spirit of the Buddhist tradition mindful hikes are offered as a dāna based event. Rick Hansen says “generosity is a beautiful practice that opens and gladdens the heart, relaxes the contraction of ‘self’ and ripples out into the world to touch many people.” The dāna practice is **heart centered** and in the spirit of generosity. Venmo or cash is graciously accepted. Venmo account is: @vickieix8; last four digits 4714 of my phone # if asked.

**No-Show Policy:** Please cancel at least 24 hours before the start of the hike. Be mindful that there may be a waitlist. If your plans change and you're not coming, opening up a spot 4-5 days before the hike it's more likely someone will be able to attend than if you cancel at the last minute. You're considered a no-show if you cancel at the last minute. Members with 2 no-shows are removed from the group.

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan
description:
Petaluma Book (And Brew) Club
2014: At a dinner for close friends and colleagues, renowned poet Francis Blundy honors his wife's birthday by reading aloud a new poem dedicated to her, 'A Corona for Vivien'. Much wine is drunk as the guests listen, and a delicious meal consumed. Little does anyone gathered around the candlelit table know that for generations to come people will speculate about the message of this poem, a copy of which has never been found, and which remains an enduring mystery. 2119: Just over one hundred years in the future, much of the western world has been submerged by rising seas following a catastrophic nuclear accident. Those who survive are haunted by the richness of the world that has been lost. In the water-logged south of what used to be England, Thomas Metcalfe, a lonely scholar and researcher, longs for the early twenty-first century as he chases the ghost of one poem, 'A Corona for Vivian'. How wild and full of risk their lives were, thinks Thomas, as he pores over the archives of that distant era, captivated by the freedoms and possibilities of human life at its zenith. When he stumbles across a clue that may lead to the elusive poem's discovery, a story is revealed of entangled loves and a brutal crime that destroy his assumptions about people he thought he knew intimately well.

title: Hunters Camp to Creekside Connector Loop - Occidental
description:
Mindfull Hikes
***Please be in good enough shape to hike at a moderate/fast steady pace (+/-2.5 mph) and comfortable with elevation changes.***

**Distance:** +/- 5.6 miles total

**The hike:** A lollipop loop near Occidental. Generally considered a moderately challenging route, with 900 ft. of elevation gain. From the trailhead the hike begins by descending down an old logging road. We'll then follow a trail until our rest area near the creek with a few simple benches.
Lots of Redwoods along the way! We'll take a trail back to the logging road/Hunters Camp trail and ascend back up to the trailhead. Note...the second half is a steady climb back up to the trailhead. This is a popular trail for hiking, mountain biking, and running.

**Parking:** is limited; Carpool if you can.

**Where to meet:** Coleman Valley Road at the gate at the trailhead. Please note that if you use the address instead of the pin for navigation it takes you past the meeting point; you'll know because there is a private property sign and no cars at that gate; turn around and come back toward Occidental about 1/3 mile.

*Please be on time. We’ll start promptly at the start time listed.* Give yourself a little extra time to arrive and get situated so that you’re part of the opening circle as this is an essential part of our time together.

No restroom available

**What to bring:** Snack, water, hat, good hiking shoes, a joyful spirit and laughter. Please dress appropriately for the weather that day. Layers of clothing are always advisable.
**===================================**
**Reminders:**
Mindful hikes are intended to be a way to connect more fully with ourselves, each other and with the land. There will be two periods of silent walking throughout the hike to allow the senses to be fully alive and felt. There will also be time during the hike to visit and connect with each other. These times of talking and connecting are an invitation to bring mindfulness to the present moment. **It's a time to put away the cell phone and cameras to disengage from technology to be fully present with each other, our *senses and the land we are inhabiting.***

***If you're on the waitlist for the hike and want to attend please message Vickie a few days before the scheduled hike. Most hikes have people drop off at the last minute and it's possible there is an opening.***

**Dāna**
In the spirit of the Buddhist tradition mindful hikes are offered as a dāna based event. Rick Hansen says “generosity is a beautiful practice that opens and gladdens the heart, relaxes the contraction of ‘self’ and ripples out into the world to touch many people.” The dāna practice is **heart centered** and in the spirit of generosity. Venmo or cash is graciously accepted. Venmo account is: @vickieix8; last four digits 4714 of my phone # if asked.

**No-Show Policy:** Please cancel at least 24 hours before the start of the hike. Be mindful that there may be a waitlist. If your plans change and you're not coming, opening up a spot 4-5 days before the hike it's more likely someone will be able to attend than if you cancel at the last minute. You're considered a no-show if you cancel at the last minute. Members with 2 no-shows will be removed from the group.

title: Spike Sikes and His Awesome Hotcakes: Salute to American Graffiti Edition
location: Hall of the Above,199 Petaluma Boulevard North, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Stick around after Cruisin' the Boulevard for this special show from Spike Sikes!

--

Like hotcakes themselves, the music Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes plays goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump.

Just The Right Recipe… The most frequently heard comment after a Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes gig goes something like this –

“No one is making this kind of music anymore!”

But what, exactly, is “this kind of music?”

Like hotcakes themselves, it goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump. It’s a sound that’s classic and simple, but when it’s done right, it hits the spot, and has you grinning from ear to ear. Spike has spent years searching for this sound.

From the Texas blues joints he cut his teeth in to the funky halls of New Orleans, he was always studying the music, trying to find just the right recipe. It makes perfect sense that he found his bandmates in Sonoma County, a music scene that has fostered many eclectic artists for decades.

What he didn’t know was how hungry audiences were for “this kind of music.” You might say they’ve been eating it up like…Hotcakes!

🍸 We will have a cash bar serving alcoholic drinks, mocktails and other beverages.

Tickets here https://www.eventbrite.com/e/spike-sikes-and-his-awesome-hotcakes-tickets-1984347404504?aff=oddtdtcreator

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

title: Afternoon at Shiloh
description:
Mindfull Hikes
***Please be in good enough shape to hike at a moderate/fast steady pace (+/-2.5 mph) and comfortable with elevation changes.***

**Distance:** +/- 4 miles
**The hike:** Join me for an afternoon hike at Shiloh Ranch Regional Park. A loop hike starting with a climb and includes: Big Leaf, Ridge, Pond and Creekside trails.

**Parking:** Park in the lot for $8 or free if you have a regional park pass.

**Where to meet:** By the Bocce court (near entrance) at Shiloh Ranch.

*Please be on time. We’ll start promptly at the start time listed.* Give yourself a little extra time to arrive and get situated so that you’re part of the opening circle as this is an essential part of our time together.

**Restroom:** At Trailhead

**What to bring:** Snack, water, hat, good hiking shoes, a joyful spirit and laughter. Please dress appropriately for the weather that day. Layers of clothing are always advisable.
**===================================**
**Reminders:**
Mindful hikes are intended to be a way to connect more fully with ourselves, each other and with the land. There will be two periods of silent walking throughout the hike to allow the senses to be fully alive and felt. There will also be time during the hike to visit and connect with each other. These times of talking and connecting are an invitation to bring mindfulness to the present moment. **It's a time to put away the cell phone and cameras to disengage from technology to be fully present with each other, our *senses and the land we are inhabiting.***

***If you're on the waitlist for the hike and want to attend please message Vickie a few days before the scheduled hike. Most hikes have people drop off at the last minute and it's possible there is an opening.***

**Dāna**
In the spirit of the Buddhist tradition mindful hikes are offered as a dāna based event. Rick Hansen says “generosity is a beautiful practice that opens and gladdens the heart, relaxes the contraction of ‘self’ and ripples out into the world to touch many people.” The dāna practice is **heart centered** and in the spirit of generosity. Venmo or cash is graciously accepted. Venmo account is: @vickieix8; last four digits 4714 of my phone # if asked.

**No-Show Policy:** Please cancel at least 24 hours before the start of the hike. Be mindful that there may be a waitlist. If your plans change and you're not coming, opening up a spot 4-5 days before the hike it's more likely someone will be able to attend than if you cancel at the last minute. You're considered a no-show if you cancel at the last minute. Members with 2 no-shows are removed from the group.

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

***Please be in good enough shape to hike at a moderate/fast steady pace (+/-2.5 mph) and comfortable with elevation changes.***

**Distance:** +/- 7.6 miles total

**The hike:** The Ridge Trail begins in the ferns and redwoods on the south fork of Matanzas Creek, then climbs through forests of oaks and bay laurels and treats hikers to stunning views of peaks surrounding Santa Rosa and Sonoma Valley. We'll go to edge of Jack London Park. This hike is an out and back.

Difficulty> Moderate

**Parking:** $8 Regional Parks fee

**Where to meet:** North Sonoma Mountain Regional Park And Open Space Preserve Parking Lot

*Please be on time. We’ll start promptly at the start time listed.* Give yourself a little extra time to arrive and get situated so that you’re part of the opening circle as this is an essential part of our time together.

Restroom at Trailhead

**What to bring:** Snack, water, hat, good hiking shoes, a joyful spirit and laughter. Please dress appropriately for the weather that day. Layers of clothing are always advisable.
***===================================***
***Reminders:***
Mindful hikes are intended to be a way to connect more fully with ourselves, each other and with the land. There will be two periods of silent walking throughout the hike to allow the senses to be fully alive and felt. There will also be time during the hike to visit and connect with each other. These times of talking and connecting are an invitation to bring mindfulness to the present moment. **It's a time to put away the cell phone and cameras to disengage from technology to be fully present with each other, our *senses and the land we are inhabiting.***

***If you're on the waitlist for the hike and want to attend please message Vickie a few days before the scheduled hike. Most hikes have people drop off at the last minute and it's possible there is an opening.***

**Dāna**
In the spirit of the Buddhist tradition mindful hikes are offered as a dāna based event. Rick Hansen says “generosity is a beautiful practice that opens and gladdens the heart, relaxes the contraction of ‘self’ and ripples out into the world to touch many people.” The dāna practice is **heart centered** and in the spirit of generosity. Venmo or cash is graciously accepted. Venmo account is: @vickieix8; last four digits 4714 of my phone # if asked.

**No-Show Policy:** Please cancel at least 24 hours before the start of the hike. Be mindful that there may be a waitlist. If your plans change and you're not coming, opening up a spot 4-5 days before the hike it's more likely someone will be able to attend than if you cancel at the last minute. You're considered a no-show if you cancel at the last minute. Members with 2 no-shows will be removed from the group.

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

description: $15 Adults, Children under 10 are free The Origin Stories Symposium is for artists and storytellers of all kinds to celebrate the power of human connection.  It's a celebration of empathy and the ways creativity can open us up to the people we pass on the street every day.  The event includes panel discussions, live music, and time to explore the art boxes  on display, illustrating their creators' personal origins. Sean Callery, tv/film composer, has received 17 Emmy nominations and 4 wins, placing him among the most nominated composers of all time. Known for his dynamic and evocative scores, he has crafted music for celebrated series such as Homeland,  R.J. Decker, The Beast in Me, the Sherlock Holmes series Elementary, Marvel’s Jessica Jones, Bones, and Designated Survivor, among others.  Tomo Moriwaki, teacher and game designer, got his start at Treyarch. A game designer for most of his career, leading the design for Spider-Man: The Movie Game (2001), Spider-Man 2: The Movie Game (2004), Boom Blox (2008), and Medal of Honor (2010). He is the Cofounder and Design Director at Hyperkinetic Studios since 2014. title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

Launch around 5:30 pm and enjoy a casual group paddle through downtown as the evening light settles over the water. We return to the dock about 30 minutes before sunset, when everyone gathers for simple snacks and conversation on the dock.

A perfect after-work outing and a great way to experience downtown Petaluma from the river.

2026 Dates: April 9 • May 14 • June 11 • July 9 • August 20 • September 24

$35 kayak or SUP rental for the duration of the paddle

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

description:
What: Kids explore the theater-making process through games and activities that build creativity, collaboration, and confidence. Each Sandcastle Drama Camp session explores a different story theme, the campers re-write the script as an ensemble to incorporate all their *original creative ideas for story, character, and design* resulting in a completely unique final play for performance each week. 

Discounts & Flexible Pricing (sliding scale) available to all. Please complete a form and we will confirm your discount code via email https://forms.gle/QixDYDky7VUUhy6b9

Who: Kids ages 6-12 

Program led by Sandcastle Theater Company's professional teaching artists
Approx. 16 students per weekly session (1:8 student/staff ratio)

Where: Polly Klaas Community Theater, 417 Western Ave. Petaluma, CA 
When: Monday – Friday, 9am – 3pm 

June 8 – 12 — make-your-own-play! Theme: The Princess & the Pea
July 6 – 10 — make-your-own-play! Theme: Alice in Wonderland
July 27 – 31 — make-your-own-play! Puss in Boots

Final Performances: Families and invited guests join us for a staged-reading/performance at 2:30pm on last day of the session.

title: Petaluma Art & Garden Festival
location: Historic Downtown Petaluma,20 4th St, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Petaluma Art & Garden Festival

The Art & Garden festival is one of Petaluma's most loved events! Join us Sunday, July 12, 2026 from 11 am to 5 pm for a fun filled day for all the family. Local crafters, artisans, gardeners, live music on two stages, and an array of local wineries, breweries, restaurants, and fine food purveyors will be participating.

The Art & Garden Festival will take place on Kentucky Street, Fourth Street, B Street, and A Street parking lot. Event Headquarters are at 20 4th Street, Petaluma.

This event is free to attend with Tasting Packages available to those who wish to partake in all the great wine, craft beer, cider, cocktails, and more.

Not the typical street fair, vendors are handpicked and will be showcasing quality, creative home and garden décor, jewelry, arts, and more. With over 100 booths of unusual, unique, handmade items, this event has something for everyone’s taste and budget.

Experts will be on hand to answer gardening questions. Figure out how to grow vegetables in tricky Petaluma adobe soil and what makes a garden organic.

While parents are eating and dancing, kids can enjoy the children’s corner, with jumpy, face painting, FREE hands-on arts and crafts, and more!

Visit http://PetalumaDowntown.com for more information!

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

title: Petaluma Fall Antique Faire
location: Downtown Petaluma,20 4th St, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Petaluma Fall Antique Faire

The much-anticipated Petaluma Fall Antique Faire returns on September 27, from 8am to 4pm, in Historic Downtown Petaluma. The Faire is located on Western Ave, the A Street Parking lot, and 4th & Kentucky Streets between B Street and Washington Street.

"The Bay Area's Premier Antique Center," Historic Downtown Petaluma will transform into an antique marketplace. Amid the beautiful historic buildings, one-of-a-kind stores, an incredible array of restaurants and cafes, guests can find an incomparable selection of affordable antiques from over 200 dealers. The show has a fantastic variety of estate jewelry, linens, furniture, art, kitchenware, vintage décor, books, and all kinds of unusual collectibles to suit everyone's budget.

Antique and collectible lovers throughout the Bay Area are welcome to browse and shop the 40th Annual Petaluma Antique Faire set in our delightful and relaxing downtown Petaluma.

This show attracts over 8k discerning collectors as well as first-time buyers wishing to collect and invest in real antiques.

Visit http://petalumadowntown.com

~ Admission is free ~

title: Santa's Riverboat Arrival & Small Business Saturday
location: River Plaza Shopping Center,54 E Washington St, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Santa's Riverboat Arrival

Saturday, November 28, 2026

11:30am - 1:30pm at River Plaza Shopping Center

Santa and Mrs. Claus are coming to town on November 28, the Saturday after Thanksgiving!

When Santa arrives in Petaluma, he leaves his sleigh at home. Instead, he and Mrs. Claus make a uniquely Petaluma arrival - they sail up the Petaluma River on a Lind Marine tugboat and dock at River Plaza Shopping Center on E. Washington to the cheers of excited children!

Starting at 11:30 am, families will enjoy live entertainment while waiting for Santa and Mrs. Claus to arrive! The Christmas couple will arrive around noon and will be welcomed by costumed dancers from the Petaluma School of Ballet’s “Nutcracker.” Santa and Mrs. Claus will make their way across the parking lot to their festive tent outside Taps Restaurant where they will be available for family photos. Be sure to bring your Christmas wish list!

Santa would love to spend all afternoon in Petaluma, but in order to hear from all the good boys and girls all over the world, he will have to be on his way to his next destination at 1:30 pm.

Don’t let the fun stop there! Keep the festive mood flowing by taking your Shop Small swag bag and make the short walk to historic downtown Petaluma to support local shopping. When we all shop small, it's not just for the things we love, but for the businesses we love, for the community we call home, and to help promote local economic growth. Learn more about Small Business Saturday http://shopsmall.com/ and visit the official Small Business Saturday Facebook https://www.facebook.com/shopsmall/ page. And take advance of shop small benefits by using your American Express card by viewing this link here https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/maps?country=US&near=Petaluma,CA&cat=Shop-Small&cl=38.232417,-122.6366524&intlink=us-GABM-Shop_Small_Map .

Visit http://PetalumaDowntown.com for more information!

title: Downtown Holiday Shopping Stroll

description:
Celebrate the season in Downtown Petaluma! Wander through festively decorated streets, discover one-of-a-kind gifts in local shops, and enjoy holiday treats, cheerful libations, live music, and extended store hours. All activities will take place inside participating businesses. Whether you’re hunting hens, shopping for loved ones, or simply soaking in the holiday spirit, there’s something fun on every corner.
